text:
alex: Heads-up — after the latest int8 quant experiment on the new llama-variant, our BERTScore numbers dropped ~4 pts vs float32 on the eval runner. Not seeing the same drop for exact-match or ROUGE.

maria: oof, any logs? is this CI-only or local repro?

alex: CI job failed a few runs: `eval-runner/8420` — attaching snippet. I repro locally on a small sample: float32 bscore=0.87, int8 bscore=0.83 for identical sentences.

alex: logs: ```
# float32
pred: "The cat sat on the mat."
ref:  "The cat is sitting on the mat."
bert_score: 0.872
# int8
bert_score: 0.829
```

dom: quick q — are we running the same tokenizer config and IDF weights in both runs? small tokenization shifts can blow up BERTScore.

alex: good call. tokenization looks identical AFAICT but the float rounding in the encoder outputs might change L2 norms. Also noticed we switched the bert-score call to `rescale_with_baseline=True` recently in the quant branch.

jen: rescale_with_baseline can be sensitive to expected model type. If the baseline was computed on a different embedding distribution it can shift calibrated scores. Can you try running raw similarity (no rescaling) to see delta?

alex: did that — raw similarity delta is ~0.03, rescaled delta is ~0.04. So rescaling amplifies it.

sylvia: CI flake: `eval-runner/8420` shows the artifact `bscore_baseline.json` differs between float and int runs (checksum mismatch). I suspect baseline caching keyed on model name + quant tag is wrong.

maria: if baseline cache uses architecture hash but not numeric dtype or quant params, int8 will pick up float32 baseline. That would explain the amplified rescale shift.

alex: here's a minimal repro snippet I used locally: ```python
from bert_score import score
preds = ["The cat sat on the mat."]
refs = ["The cat is sitting on the mat."]
# embeddings from our encoder (simulated)
emb_float = get_embeddings(preds, dtype='float32')
emb_int8 = quantize_and_dequantize(emb_float, scheme='sym')
print(score(preds, refs, model_type='our-bert', verbose=False))
# replace rescale_with_baseline with False/True to see effect
```

dom: simple fixes: (1) include dtype+quant-hash in baseline cache key, (2) add regression test that runs float->quant and asserts bscore(delta) < 0.02 without rescaling, (3) make rescale_with_baseline opt-in in our runner config.

maria: agree. also add a unit that loads the canonical bert-score baseline from the external repo so we don't accidentally drift.

jen: I'll open a small PR for (1) and (3). Can someone own the regression test?

alex: I can add the regression harness — will add a synthetic pair and run both float32 and quant across CPU/GPU to catch CI flakiness. Plan: add test to `eval/integration/metrics_regression.py` and mark it smoke so it runs on PRs.

sylvia: CI bot shows the failing job details: <https://ci.internal/runs/8420|eval-runner/8420> — tags: @jen @alex @dom

ci-bot: Job eval-runner/8420 failed: bertscore_regression (flake). Logs saved at arn:ci:artifacts:8420/bert_logs.tar.gz

jen: thx. alex — can you paste the exact baseline-cache key change? small patch idea: ```diff
- baseline_key = f"{model_name}:{version}"
+ baseline_key = f"{model_name}:{version}:{dtype}:{quant_hash}"
```

alex: yep that's the one. I'll include quant_hash derived from the quant config json. Also will add a comment in the cache module.

maria: reminder: add an eval-perf note in release notes that quant can change embedding norms and therefore some calibration flows must be re-run.

alex: will do. PR incoming in ~30m. if CI passes we can merge and then re-run the failing eval job to regen baselines. :+1:

dom: great. after merge, let's run a small sweep across a couple of models to ensure no accidental regressions (bert-base, our-bert, llama-embed).

jen: assign me for code review. thanks all.
